title: Hybridization of Random-Primed DNA Probes
author: Jonathan Houseley
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bns8mehw

steps.title: Check hybridization bottles
steps.instruction: Inspect hybridization bottles and internal seals for damage to prevent radioactive buffer leakage during hybridization.

steps.title: Prewarm ULTRAHyb buffer
steps.instruction: Place a bottle of ULTRAHyb in a 68 °C oven and warm until the SDS fully dissolves (approximately 15–20 min).

steps.title: Prepare membrane in hybridization bottle
steps.instruction: Wet the membrane with 0.1× SSC containing 0.1 % SDS, roll it up RNA‑face inward, drop it into the pre‑warmed ULTRAHyb bottle and slowly rotate the bottle to unroll the membrane against the bottle wall; use a Stripette to assist, push out air bubbles, and balance the bottle (including liquid volume) in the rotisserie oven. Verify correct orientation (visible edge must move with rotation; a thin cigar shape indicates reversal). Two membranes may be placed in one bottle, one facing the glass and the other the bottle interior.

steps.title: Prehybridize membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in 7.5 mL ULTRAHyb at 42 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Prepare DNA labeling reaction
steps.instruction: Dilute 25 ng DNA template to a final volume of 37 µL with water in a screw‑cap tube.

steps.title: Label DNA probe
steps.instruction: Heat the DNA solution at 100 °C for 5 min, then snap‑chill on ice water for 2–3 min and centrifuge briefly. Add 10 µL 5× labeling buffer, 1 µL Klenow (exo‑) enzyme, and 2 µL [α‑32P] dCTP. Mix by pipetting and incubate at 37 °C for 1–3 hours.

steps.title: Purify labeled probe via Quick Spin column
steps.instruction: Clean the probe using a mini Quick Spin column as follows:

substeps.instruction: Flick the column inverted then right‑side up to settle the sepharose at the bottom; remove the top and bottom caps per product instructions.
Place the column in a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube and spin at 1000 × g for 30 s (temperature unspecified). Discard the tube and transfer the column to a new 1.5 mL screw‑cap tube.
Dilute the probe with water to a total volume of 50 µL and carefully pipette onto the centre of the sepharose matrix.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 4 min (temperature unspecified).

steps.title: Assess labeling efficiency
steps.instruction: Hold the probe‑containing column and the eluate at equal distances from a Geiger counter using tweezers; at least 50 % of the radioactivity should be in the eluate (equal Geiger reading). Discard the column to radioactive waste.

steps.title: Denature probe
steps.instruction: Heat the purified probe at 100 °C for 5 min, then snap‑chill on ice water for 2–3 min and centrifuge briefly.

steps.title: Hybridize probe to membrane
steps.instruction: Add the denatured probe vertically into the hybridization bottle so it falls directly into the ULTRAHyb buffer and incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 42 °C.

steps.title: Dispose of probe solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the remaining probe solution into a 50 mL Falcon/Corning tube and discard; reuse of random‑primed probes is not recommended.

steps.title: Low stringency wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with 6× SSC for 10 min at 42 °C.

steps.title: High stringency wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with pre‑heated 2× SSC containing 0.1 % SDS for 10 min at 42 °C.

steps.title: Final wash and optional extra wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane for 10 min with 50 mL 6× SSC at room temperature. Optionally, perform two additional washes of 30 min each with 2× SSC containing 0.5 % SDS at 42 °C to reduce background (may also reduce signal).
